# Wazwan Way

> Wazwan Way (wazwanway.com) is a guide to Kashmiri food and travel. It explains Wazwan, Kashmir's formal multi-course feast, and the wider cuisine around it: dishes, breads, tea, street food, history and etiquette. It also lists restaurants in Srinagar, destinations across Kashmir, scenic drives and a trip planner.

Wazwan is cooked by teams of master chefs called wazas and eaten by four diners sharing a copper platter called the trami. Its size varies: 36 courses is the traditional ideal, while a 2016 review in the Journal of Ethnic Foods puts Wazwan at anywhere from 7 to 36 dishes. The popular story that Wazwan began with cooks from Samarkand who came to Kashmir in Timur's time is the wazas' own account rather than recorded history: Timur never entered Kashmir, and no document records how the feast began.

## Wazwan

- [Traditional Wazwan](https://wazwanway.com/dishes): The main page on Wazwan: what the feast is, its dishes in serving order, the wazas who cook it, what is documented about its history, how many dishes it has, and how to try it, with sources
- [How Wazwan Is Served](https://wazwanway.com/kashmiri-food/wazwan/guide/how-wazwan-is-served): The trami, the hand-washing, the serving order and the etiquette
- [History of Wazwan](https://wazwanway.com/kashmiri-food/wazwan/guide/history-of-wazwan): The Timur story, what the historical record shows, and how the feast took shape
- [What Does Waza Mean?](https://wazwanway.com/kashmiri-food/wazwan/guide/waza-meaning): The professional cooks behind Wazwan and the vasta waza who leads them
- [How Much Does Wazwan Cost?](https://wazwanway.com/kashmiri-food/wazwan/guide/cost-guide): What Wazwan costs in a restaurant and at a wedding, with dated figures and what drives them
- [Vegetarian Wazwan](https://wazwanway.com/kashmiri-food/wazwan/guide/vegetarian-wazwan): Which Wazwan dishes are vegetarian, how they are made, and what to eat at a wedding or restaurant
- [Restaurant vs Wedding vs Home](https://wazwanway.com/kashmiri-food/wazwan/guide/restaurant-vs-wedding-vs-home): What changes between a wedding Wazwan, a restaurant Wazwan and Kashmiri home cooking
- [How to Experience Wazwan](https://wazwanway.com/how-to-experience): A first-timer's guide
- [Rista vs Gushtaba](https://wazwanway.com/kashmiri-food/wazwan/guide/rista-vs-gushtaba): The two pounded-meatball dishes compared
- [Gushtaba and Tabak Maaz GI Tags](https://wazwanway.com/kashmiri-food/wazwan/guide/gi-tag-gushtaba-tabak-maaz): Where the 2024 GI applications for the two Wazwan dishes stand, from the GI Registry's records
- [How Many Calories Are in a Wazwan?](https://wazwanway.com/kashmiri-food/wazwan/guide/wazwan-calories): The one published count, a 2012 Srinagar wedding studied by SKIMS researchers, dish by dish, and a 2026 health advisory's estimate
- [Wazwan vs Mughlai Cuisine](https://wazwanway.com/kashmiri-food/wazwan/guide/wazwan-vs-mughlai): How Kashmir's feast differs from the Mughlai cooking of northern India, with sources
- [All Wazwan guides](https://wazwanway.com/kashmiri-food/wazwan/guide)

## Wazwan dishes

Each dish page has what the dish is, its place in the feast and a recipe, with sources.

- [Tabak Maaz](https://wazwanway.com/dishes/tabak-maaz): Twice-cooked lamb ribs, served first on the trami
- [Rista](https://wazwanway.com/dishes/rista): Pounded mutton meatballs in a red gravy
- [Rogan Josh](https://wazwanway.com/dishes/rogan-josh): The Kashmiri Muslim and Pandit versions, and why there's no tomato
- [Daniwal Korma](https://wazwanway.com/dishes/daniwal-korma): Mutton in a yogurt gravy with fresh coriander
- [Marchwangan Korma](https://wazwanway.com/dishes/marchwangan-korma): Mutton in a hot gravy of Kashmiri red chillies
- [Aab Gosht](https://wazwanway.com/dishes/aab-gosht): Mutton cooked in milk
- [Yakhni](https://wazwanway.com/dishes/yakhni): Mutton in a yogurt gravy with fennel, the last gravy before gushtaba
- [Gushtaba](https://wazwanway.com/dishes/gushtaba): The large pounded meatball in yogurt gravy that ends the main meal
- [The core seven: a story for each essential Wazwan dish](https://wazwanway.com/blog/core-seven): The series page for the seven long-form dish stories below, in the order they come to the trami, with how they were researched
- [Rogan Josh: history, name and colour](https://wazwanway.com/blog/rogan-josh-history): Where the dish came from, what its name means, why it is red without tomatoes, and the Kashmiri Muslim and Pandit versions
- [Gushtaba: why the Wazwan ends with it](https://wazwanway.com/blog/gushtaba-last-dish-of-wazwan): What its name means, how wazas pound it from fresh-killed mutton, its yakhni gravy, and its place as the last dish
- [Tabak Maaz: ribs cooked twice](https://wazwanway.com/blog/tabak-maaz-ribs-cooked-twice): What the name means, the two cookings, the milk-or-water question, how it differs from kabargah, and the GI application
- [Rista: the meatball pounded on a stone](https://wazwanway.com/blog/rista-pounded-meatballs): How wazas pound it from fresh mutton, what colours its gravy, how it differs from gushtaba and where it comes in the meal
- [Aab Gosht: the milk curry of the Wazwan](https://wazwanway.com/blog/aab-gosht-milk-curry): What the name means, the ten litres reduced to one, which cut is used, and how it differs from Persian abgoosht
- [Daniwal Korma: the coriander course](https://wazwanway.com/blog/daniwal-korma-coriander): What its name means, what korma means in Kashmir, how it is made, and where it comes in the meal
- [Marchwangan Korma: the hottest dish on the trami](https://wazwanway.com/blog/marchwangan-korma-chilli): What its name means, how much Kashmiri chilli goes in, how it differs from rogan josh and where it comes in the meal
